name: Utah Summer Agriculture Program (Supervised Agricultural Experience)
org: Utah State Board of Education, Career and Technical Education
what_you_do: Do a summer farm project. You can raise animals, work at a farm business, run a small farm business or do service. Your ag teacher visits and tracks your work in an online tracker.
who_can_apply: Incoming 9th to 12th graders enrolled in an approved agriculture class for the next school year, with an approved SAE plan. High school graduates are not eligible. Your school must run a Summer Ag Program.
pay_detail: The program itself is school based. Projects can be paid or unpaid, and your employer may pay you for SAE work. School credit may be offered.
duration: Starts the day after the school contract ends and runs to the day before the next one starts
deadline_text: Teachers send in their plan and roster April 15 to 30 each year. Ask your ag teacher when to sign up.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school agriculture teacher. You need an approved SAE plan in the Agricultural Experience Tracker (AET). Use your boundary school's Summer Ag Program. If that is not available, you can work with a school in the same district with parent consent and approval.
notes: The guide is written for teachers and districts. Each program needs at least 35 students and a licensed ag teacher, so not every school has one. Ask your ag teacher.
